text:
The largest crypto hack on record had a contained market impact. That is worth understanding.

The Binance exploit was $6.3bn. Approximately $2.8bn in stolen assets was frozen quickly by Circle, Tether and other issuers. The exploit represented a small part of Binance's $171bn in customer assets.

In plain terms: because transactions on public blockchains are visible, issuers could trace the stolen funds and freeze them. A traditional institution rarely gets that kind of visibility in the first hours of an incident.

For allocators, the question is less whether incidents happen and more how quickly exposure can be seen and acted on. That is the theme of the risk framework we published with Clear Street, which breaks DeFi exposure into chain, protocol and asset layers.

Our curated vaults had no exposure to the event.

This week's Weekly sets out the full picture: [link]
